title: Celebrating Realism
description: National call at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania for work made in the realist tradition. The prospectus traces the thread from Gustave Courbet's Realist Manifesto - everyday people, activities and objects, nature shown with its irregularities, idealised figures and romanticised fantasies rejected - through the twentieth and twenty-first century movements that grew out of it: Photorealism, Social Realism, New Objectivity, American Regionalism and Hyperrealism. The gallery asks how you observe and record perceived reality, how you organise pictorial elements, embrace precision, manipulate light and modify colour tonalities while keeping emotion in the work. There is no restriction on subject matter: landscapes, cityscapes, still lifes, events, special occasions, man-made environments, animals and people are all invited. Artists, photographers and sculptors at every level may enter, all photographic processes are welcome, and there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over. Entry is $35 for three images and $5 for each additional image up to nine. Jurying is by an anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers and academics. Awards are an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery second room, an optional $200 Director Choice award, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from everyone shown at the gallery during the year. Work must be wired for hanging, no larger than 48 inches framed and under 50 lbs, sculpture no larger than 28 inches; photographs should be framed in black or white with white or off-white mats if presented traditionally, and plexiglass is preferred over glass for shipped pieces. Accepted work must arrive by 23 February 2027. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping and insurance both ways with a prepaid return label. Exhibition runs 28 February to 26 March 2027.
jury: Anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, curators & academics
summary: Realism in all its forms at MVA Gallery, Bethlehem PA. All photographic processes welcome; $200 and an NYC exhibition.
prose: Realism calls can be quietly hostile to photography - the assumption being that a camera does realism automatically, so there is nothing left to judge. MVA Gallery does not read it that way. The prospectus opens with Courbet's Realist Manifesto and its insistence that artists portray everyday people, activities and objects, that nature be depicted with its irregularities, and that idealised figures and romanticised fantasies be refused. It then traces what grew from that: Photorealism, Social Realism, New Objectivity, American Regionalism, Hyperrealism - movements the gallery describes as a rebellion against Abstractionism, still taking new forms and using current technologies.

The questions the call actually asks are craft questions, and they apply as squarely to a photographer as to a painter: how do you observe and record perceived reality, how do you organise pictorial elements, embrace precision, manipulate light and modify colour tonalities while keeping emotion in the work. There is no restriction on subject matter - landscapes, cityscapes, still lifes, events, special occasions, man-made environments, animals, people. The mediums line names photography alongside painting, watercolour, printmaking, mixed media, digital, pastel, encaustic, ink, sculpture, fibre and drawing, and the artwork specifications close with the sentence that matters: all photographic processes are welcome. There is no cutoff date for when the work was made.

MVA - Modern Visual Arts - is a physical gallery in the historic Moravian quarter of Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, an hour from New York City. Entry is $35 for three images and $5 for each additional image up to nine, open to US residents aged 18 and over, and jurying is by a small rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers and academics who have asked to remain anonymous for this exhibit. The award ladder is the one MVA runs across its programme: an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery second room, an optional $200 Director Choice award, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of one New York City exhibition opportunity drawn in December from everyone shown that calendar year. Work must be wired, no sawtooth hangers, under 48 inches framed and 50 lbs, with plexiglass preferred for anything shipped. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists pay shipping and insurance both ways with a prepaid return label enclosed. Entries close 30 September 2026, notification is on or about 20 January 2027, accepted work must arrive by 23 February, and the exhibition runs 28 February to 26 March 2027.

title: 37 Memorial María Luisa
fee: First photo free, then €22 for everything else; free for entrants under 19 and for photographers with disabilities
description: Long-running international contest for mountain, nature and adventure photography and film, run from Infiesto in Asturias by friends of María Luisa Álvarez, who died in a mountain accident in 1990, and financed by them. The 37th edition has fourteen photographic categories - Mountain Landscape, Alpinism, Climbing, Adventure and Extreme Sports, Man in the Mountain and/or Nature, Animal World, The World of Birds, Vegetal World, Submerged World, Biodiversity and Geodiversity, Nature Landscapes, Creative Photo, Macro Picture, and a Topic of the Year which for this edition is The Universe - plus a category for videos, films and documentaries. For the first time the Memorial also runs a special section for photographers with disabilities. Amateurs and professionals anywhere may enter. The first photograph is free; everything after that is covered by a single €22 payment including VAT that unlocks all categories and the video section, and participation is free for photographers with disabilities and for entrants under 19. Each author may submit up to five photographs per category. Files are JPEG, 1,920 pixels on the longest side, maximum 2 MB, Adobe RGB 1998 preferred, with no frames, borders or captions added; multiple exposure is allowed if registered in camera in a single primary file, and HDR and panoramas are accepted. Judging is anonymous: the system assigns every photograph an alphanumeric code and the panel, drawn by the Founders Board from mountain and nature photographers of recognised prestige, never sees the author. The overall winner takes €5,000, a trophy, a diploma, a book portfolio and two invitations to the awards gala; each of the fourteen category winners takes €300 and the same trophy, diploma, portfolio and invitations. There is a Young Photographers Prize and an Award for the person with a disability, each a Samsung 5G tablet with trophy, diploma, portfolio and invitations, a Citizen watch for the Topic of the Year, and a €3,000 FotoRuano voucher for the best video, film or documentary, with honourable mentions at the panel's discretion. Results are published on 1 March 2027 and the gala is held on 23 and 24 April 2027 in Infiesto and Oviedo, with free accommodation for the winner and a companion. Selected work joins the Memorial's touring exhibition, which is lent framed, labelled and crated to non-profit mountain and environmental organisations.
requirements: Up to 5 photos per category (70 max)

prose: The Memorial María Luisa is not a brand exercise. It is run from Infiesto, in the Asturian interior, by a group of friends of María Luisa Álvarez, who died in a mountain accident on 18 November 1990, and the FAQ answers the question of who the organisers are in one line: some of María Luisa's friends, who are very keen on mountains, and who finance the contest. Thirty-seven editions later it still opens in September and closes on 1 December, and photographers and filmmakers from more than a hundred countries have entered it.

The structure is unusually generous for a contest this size. The first photograph is free. Everything after that is covered by a single €22 payment, VAT included, that unlocks all fourteen photographic categories and the video section together - and participation is free outright for entrants under 19 and, for the first time this year, for photographers with disabilities, who also have a section and an award of their own. The categories run from Mountain Landscape, Alpinism and Climbing through Adventure and Extreme Sports, Man in the Mountain and/or Nature, Animal World, The World of Birds, Vegetal World, Submerged World, Biodiversity and Geodiversity, Nature Landscapes, Creative Photo and Macro, to a Topic of the Year that is The Universe for this edition. You may enter five photographs in each. Multiple exposure counts if it was registered in camera in a single primary file; HDR and panoramas are fine.

Judging is genuinely blind - the system assigns each photograph an alphanumeric code the moment it arrives, and the panel, drawn by the Founders Board from mountain and nature photographers of recognised prestige, never sees who made it. The overall winner receives €5,000, a trophy, a diploma, a book portfolio and two invitations to the gala; each of the fourteen category winners receives €300 and the same trophy, diploma, portfolio and invitations. There is a Samsung 5G tablet for the Young Photographers Prize and another for the Award for the person with a disability, a Citizen watch for the Topic of the Year, and a €3,000 FotoRuano voucher for the best video, film or documentary. Results are announced on 1 March 2027 and the prize gala runs 23-24 April 2027 in Infiesto and Oviedo, with accommodation provided free for the winner and a companion. Selected work then joins the Memorial's touring exhibition, which the organisers lend - framed, labelled and crated - to non-profit mountain and environmental groups.

title: SE Center for Photography — The Portrait
description: The SE Center takes the portrait from classic to contemporary, framing it as an object of remembrance and reverence, of seduction and glorification - from the keepsake in a locket to the likeness of a leader meant to inspire, from the image that confronts and drives us to action to the one that lulls us into longing for a time since passed. The call describes the portrait as both a mirror, in whose reflection we find the inward experiences of ourselves, and a window from which we look out toward the virtues of another. Analog and digital manipulation in all its forms is welcome, monochrome or colour, all subjects, analog, digital or antique processes, and photographers of every skill level and location may enter. The juror is Aline Smithson, the Los Angeles artist, educator and editor known for conceptual portraiture that uses humour and pathos to explore the performative potential of photography; she has had more than forty solo shows, has taught at the Los Angeles Center of Photography since 2001, and founded Lenscratch in 2007. Thirty-five to forty images hang in the SE Center's virtual gallery for about a month, with the selection also carried across the Center's social channels, an archived online slideshow and a video walkthrough. Entry is $35 for up to five images and $6 for each additional image to a maximum of fifteen, with member rates of $28 and $5. Work exhibited at the SE Center within the previous two years is not eligible. The Center takes no commission - the artist keeps 100 percent of any sale. The exhibition runs 15 December 2026 to 30 January 2027.
jury: Aline Smithson, artist, educator and founder of Lenscratch

org: Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum
description: HIPA runs this global competition with the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the 2026 United Nations Water Conference, which the UAE and Senegal co-host in Abu Dhabi from 8 to 10 December 2026. The brief starts from the observation that water is experienced differently across people, communities and environments, and that photography can make those experiences visible - documenting challenges, celebrating solutions and connecting global conversations to real human stories. Entrants submit a story of five to ten photographs exploring the relationship between water and people, communities, the planet, innovation, or challenges. Entry is free and open to individuals aged 18 and over anywhere in the world; submissions run from 16 September to 15 October 2026 at 23:59 UAE time and are made only through the members area of the HIPA site. A title and description for the portfolio are required. Files must be JPEG of at least 5 MB, no less than 2,000 pixels on the longest edge and 300 dpi, and the original RAW or unedited file must be uploaded alongside; phone and drone photographs are allowed. No tags, signatures, initials, frames, borders, logos or other added marks are permitted. Basic technical editing is acceptable so long as it does not affect the authenticity of the photograph, but advanced editing used to create illusions, deceptions or manipulations - including compositing and creative retouching - is prohibited. The prizes are $10,000 for first place, $8,000 for second and $5,000 for third. Winners provide bank and personal details within seven days of request and are paid within two months of the results. Finalists and winners grant HIPA a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, sub-licensable licence to use the submitted work in connection with the competition and HIPA's own promotion, and entrants must be able to supply model, property and copyright releases on request.
summary: HIPA, the UAE foreign ministry and the 2026 UN Water Conference want a 5–10 picture story about water. Free, $10,000 top prize.
prose: Water conferences generate a lot of paper and not much looking. This one is trying to do something about that. HIPA - the Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum International Photography Award - has partnered with the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the 2026 United Nations Water Conference, which the UAE and Senegal co-host in Abu Dhabi from 8 to 10 December, and is asking photographers worldwide for a story of five to ten pictures about how water shapes our world and the people who depend on it.

The five suggested axes are water and people, water and communities, water and planet, water and innovation, water and challenges - broad enough to take a documentary project on a drying river, a portrait series about a fishing town, or work on desalination and irrigation technology. Entry is free, open to anyone 18 or over, and the window is short: submissions opened on 16 September 2026 and close on 15 October at 23:59 UAE time, through the members area of the HIPA site. You submit a titled, described portfolio rather than single frames.

The technical bar is high and the authenticity rules are strict. Files must be JPEG of at least 5 MB, no less than 2,000 pixels on the longest edge at 300 dpi, and you upload the original RAW or unedited file alongside. Phone and drone photographs are allowed; tags, signatures, frames, borders and logos are not. Basic technical editing is fine, but advanced editing used to create illusions, deceptions or manipulations - compositing and creative retouching are named - is prohibited. Prizes are $10,000, $8,000 and $5,000, paid within two months of the announcement. Worth reading before you enter: finalists and winners grant HIPA a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free and sub-licensable licence over the submitted work for competition and HIPA promotional use, and you must be able to produce model, property and copyright releases within seven days if asked.

title: Dek Unu Magazine — January 2027 Issue
description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome - each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview, and there is no word limit on the artist's own account of the work. The jurors read the documents as well as the images, and the magazine says it looks for coherent, intentional art, straight to strange, alongside technical excellence. The submission window for the January issue runs November 1-20, 2026, with the magazine closed for jury from the 21st to the 1st of the following month; submissions are by a single email carrying 11 separately named images plus bio and project commentary. Entrants must be at least 18, and submission is limited to artists not previously published by Dek Unu. Dek Unu charges no fee to submit and does not pay contributors; copyright in the images always remains with the artist.
summary: Not-for-profit journal publishing one artist per issue in print and online. January issue window November 1–20. Free.

title: Things That Go Bump in the Art
fee: Free (Berkeley Arts Council membership required, from $15)
description: Halloween-themed member exhibit in the back gallery at Berkeley Art Works, the Berkeley Arts Council's space in downtown Martinsburg, West Virginia. The council is calling for artists of the spooky, gothic, medieval, dark, strange and quirky, and says glow-in-the-dark work is especially encouraged. The call does not enumerate media - it asks for artwork rather than naming photography, painting or anything else - but the council's programme is all-media, its annual Eastern West Virginia juried exhibition accepting original two- or three-dimensional work in any medium or technique. Work must be ready to hang and no larger than 24 by 24 inches, with smaller pieces preferred because the back gallery is small; three-dimensional work may be considered if it can be hung or sits on a shelf, and larger pieces may be turned away for lack of space. There is no entry fee and no submission platform: this is a members-only show and work is hand-delivered to the gallery at 116 North Queen Street between 24 and 27 September 2026. Membership can be bought at the point of entry and runs $35 individual, $25 senior and $15 youth or student, with entering exhibitions listed among member benefits. The exhibit runs 1 to 31 October 2026 and culminates in a Halloween reception and costume party on 31 October from 8 to 10 PM, where guests act as judges and vote for a Best Loved award. There is no jury and no cash prize. Proceeds and donations support the council's work connecting artists, audiences and local businesses across Berkeley County.
summary: Spooky, gothic and strange work for a free members' Halloween show at Berkeley Art Works. Hand delivery, 24 inches max.
